title: Protocol for examining the capability of senescent tumor cells to stimulate murine bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells by flow cytometry
protocol: Obtain femurs from a 7–9-week BALB/c mouse.
Spray mouse surface with 70% ethanol after it has been euthanized according to the institution’s protocol.
Dissect out both femurs without breaking the epiphyses, and carefully remove the muscle and fibrous tissues without damaging the bones.
Use a Kimwipe saturated with 70% ethanol to remove excess muscle if necessary.
Remove soft tissue surrounding the femur to expose the epiphysis.
Dissect the femur from the epiphysis using a sharp and fine dissection scissor.
Rinse the bones in 70% ethanol.
Wash the bones in ice-cold sterile PBS to remove ethanol.
Transfer the bones into a sterile Petri dish containing 7 mL of basic immune cell medium.
Cut off both epiphyses using sterile scissors.
Hold the bone with forceps while flushing the marrow into the Petri dish.
Flush the bone from both ends and scrape its inner surfaces with a needle as needed.
Transfer all cells from the Petri dish through a 40 μm strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Wash the Petri dish and strainer twice with 7 mL basic immune cell medium to collect remaining cells.
Discard the strainer.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of 1× Red Blood Cell (RBC) Lysis Buffer and incubate on ice for 5–10 min with occasional shaking.
Add 20–30 mL of basic immune cell medium to stop the reaction.
Pellet cells by centrifuging at 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL DC medium.
Count cells and adjust to 2×10^6 viable cells/mL.
Mix 10 μL cell suspension and 10 μL trypan blue for staining dead cells.
Load 10 μL of the mixture onto a hemocytometer for manual counting.
Transfer cell suspension from Falcon tube into a T75 flask.
Place the flask in a regular cell culture incubator.
Differentiate bone marrow cells into CD11c+/CD103+ DCs in the presence of Flt3 ligand (200 ng/mL) and GM-CSF (1 ng/mL).
On Day 6, transfer half of the cell suspension (10–15 mL) into a sterile Falcon tube.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellets in fresh DC medium and place them back in the old flask.
On Day 9, gently tap the flask to harvest non-adherent cells.
Count the harvested cell number.
Calculate the total volume of cell suspension required based on the target density of 3×10^6 viable cells/mL.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Remove sufficient supernatant to leave the cells at twice the target density.
Dilute the DCs to 3×10^6 cells/mL by adding an equal volume of fresh DC medium and resuspend the cell pellet by gently pipetting.
Transfer the entire cell suspension to a new T75 flask and return it to the incubator.
Adjust the suspension to 2–3 × 10^6 viable cells/mL if the cell count is low, and move the cells to a smaller flask corresponding to the final volume.
Perform another DC medium change on Day 12 as described above.
Phenotype CD103+ DCs on Day 14.
Examine DC morphology under a phase contrast microscope prior to harvesting.
Gently tap the flask and transfer 2 mL of cell suspension into a FACS tube.
Count cells and make an aliquot of 3×10^5 viable cells for surface staining in a new FACS tube.
Add 1 mL PBS to the FACS tube with 3×10^5 viable cells.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 100 μL PBS containing Zombie Yellow diluted at 1:2000.
Incubate for 15 min at ∼23°C in the dark.
Optional: Add 0.5 μg anti-mouse CD16/32 antibody to the Zombie Yellow live/dead staining buffer to block Fc receptors.
Add 2 mL of Cell Staining Buffer, centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min, and discard the supernatant.
Stain the surface proteins with the following antibody panel in a final volume of 100 μL.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min in the dark.
Wash samples with 1 mL of Cell Staining Buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 300 μL Cell Staining Buffer.
Analyze by flow cytometry.
Pause point: Keep freshly stained cells at 4°C in the dark for up to 2 h before analysis.
Fix cells in 2% PFA for 15 min at approximately 23°C.
Wash fixed cells once with PBS.
Resuspend fixed cells in 300 μL of Cell Staining Buffer.
Store fixed cells at 4°C in the dark for up to a week before analysis.
Maintain CT26 cells.
Prewarm complete RPMI medium, PBS, and trypsin-EDTA in a 37°C bead bath.
Passage cells once they have reached 80%-90% confluence.
Remove the cell culture medium and rinse the cells once with PBS.
Add 4 mL of trypsin-EDTA to the T75 flask and rock gently to cover cells completely.
Incubate the flask at 37°C for approximately 2 min.
Once the cells have detached, add 8 mL of pre-warmed complete RPMI medium and disperse the cells by pipetting gently.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 300 × g for 5 min if sensitive to trypsin-EDTA.
Discard the supernatant to remove residual trypsin-EDTA.
Resuspend the cells in complete RPMI medium after discarding the supernatant.
Transfer 1/4–1/8 volumes of cell suspension to a new T75 flask and add 15 mL of complete RPMI medium.
Return the cells to the incubator.
Seed 2.5 × 10^4 CT26 cells with 1 mL medium in each well of a 12-well plate and allow them to attach overnight (12–16 h).
Add etoposide or GSK461364 to a final concentration of 2 μM.
Apply an equal amount of DMSO vehicle to control cells.
Culture the cells in the presence of senescence inducers for 5 days.
Seed cells at an appropriate density for senescence induction, aiming for 30%–50% confluence at the time of drug treatment.
Prevent cells from overgrowing prior to entering senescence by adjusting cell seeding density.
Maintain medium without changing it during the 5-day incubation period for senescence induction.
Supplement or replace medium if necessary, ensuring added medium contains the same concentration of senescence inducers or DMSO vehicle.
Induce senescence in CT26 cells by treating them with etoposide (2 μM) or GSK461364 (2 μM) for 5 days.
Use CT26 cells treated with DMSO vehicle as controls.
Obtain representative phase-contrast images of the treated cells.
Perform SA-β-Gal staining on CT26 cells.
Remove cell culture medium and gently wash cells once with PBS.
Fix cells in 2% PFA for 3–5 min.
Stain cells overnight (12–16 h) at 37°C with prewarmed SA-β-Gal staining solution.
Gently wash the cells twice with PBS prewarmed to 37°C.
Keep the stained cells in PBS for imaging under a microscope with a color camera.
Store stained cells at 4°C in the dark for up to two weeks before imaging.
Alternatively, store stained cells in 70% glycerol in the dark at 4°C for longer periods.
Maintain senescent tumor cells in basic immune cell medium after removing senescence inducers.
Induce CT26 cell senescence as described above.
Treat control cells with DMSO vehicle.
Prepare cells in duplicate.
Examine cell morphology under a microscope.
Wash cells twice with 2 mL sterile PBS.
Collect cells from one sample for counting.
Replace PBS with 1.5 mL fresh basic immune cell medium.
Return cells to the incubator.
Maintain senescent cells in basic immune cell medium for 4 h–16 h before coculturing with BMDCs.
Coculture BMDCs with SnCs.
Collect DCs in sterile tubes and centrifuge them for 5 min at 300 × g.
Decant the medium after centrifugation.
Resuspend DCs in fresh immune cell medium.
Count viable cells.
Adjust the concentration to 0.5×10^6 viable cells/mL.
Add BMDCs to SnCs at an approximate ratio of 2:1.
Culture adherent senescent cells in a 12-well plate, producing approximately 0.5 × 10^5 SnCs per well.
Introduce around 1×10^5 BMDCs in 200 μL per well into the 12-well plate for coculture experiments.
Maintain a 2:1 ratio of BMDCs to senescent or non-senescent cells when performing cocultures.
Return cells to the incubator and culture overnight (12–16 h).
Supplement the medium with GM-CSF at a final concentration of 0.2 ng/mL during coculture.
Add Flt3 ligand to the medium at a final concentration of 40 ng/mL during coculture.
Expose BMDCs to senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) during coculture.
Allow BMDCs to take up SnC membranes and cytoplasm via phagocytosis or trogocytosis.
Use unstimulated BMDCs as a negative control.
Stimulate BMDCs with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 2 μg/mL to serve as a positive control.
Harvest CD103+ BMDCs into FACS tubes.
Gently pipette the cocultured cells up and down.
Transfer all the suspended cells to a FACS tube.
Rinse the well with 1 mL of PBS to collect the remaining cells.
Pellet the cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Decant the supernatant.
Stain the BMDCs for flow cytometric analysis.
Resuspend cell pellets in 100 μL PBS containing Zombie Yellow diluted at 1:2000 and 0.5 μg anti-mouse CD16/32 antibody.
Incubate for 15 min at approximately 23°C in the dark.
Add 2 mL of Cell Staining Buffer to the FACS tube to wash the cells.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Prepare the surface protein staining solution as follows.
Add 100 μL of staining solution to each sample.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min in the dark.
For washing cells, add 2 mL of Cell Staining Buffer to the FACS tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min and carefully discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 300 μL Cell Staining Buffer.
Analyze the cells by flow cytometry.
